lab_title: The Heart: Structure and the Path of Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart and their spatial relationships
Identify the four valves of the heart and describe their function in preventing backflow
Identify the major vessels entering and leaving the heart
Trace the dual-loop (pulmonary and systemic) circulation pathway through the heart
Explain the structural difference between right and left ventricle myocardium in relation to their functional demands

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce students to the external anatomy of the heart and orient them to anterior, posterior, superior, and inferior views before diving into internal structures.
key_visuals: A rotating, life-size 3D heart model floating in space
Labeled anterior and posterior surfaces
Color-coded regions hinting at chambers beneath the surface
student_actions: Rotate and zoom the 3D heart model
Tap on anterior and posterior surfaces to reveal orientation labels
Answer a quick orientation quiz identifying superior vs inferior aspects

scenes.brief_purpose: Guide students to identify and locate the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle, establishing the internal chamber layout.
key_visuals: Cutaway view of the heart exposing all four internal chambers
Color-coded chambers (blue for deoxygenated side, red for oxygenated side)
Interior chamber walls with visible thickness differences
student_actions: Tap each chamber to reveal its name and function
Drag labels to match the correct chamber
Complete a matching exercise identifying chamber locations

scenes.brief_purpose: Highlight the structural difference between the right and left ventricle myocardium and connect this to their differing pumping demands.
key_visuals: Side-by-side cross-section slicing through both ventricles
Measurement overlay showing wall thickness in millimeters
Visual comparison of pulmonary loop (short) vs systemic loop (long) distances
student_actions: Slide a comparison tool across the cross-section to measure wall thickness
Select the correct explanation for why the left ventricle wall is thicker
Reflect via short-answer prompt on pressure requirements of each loop

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves and their role in maintaining one-way blood flow.
key_visuals: Transparent heart model with valves highlighted at chamber junctions
Animated valve opening and closing during a simulated heartbeat
Close-up inset views of valve leaflets/cusps
student_actions: Tap each valve to see its name and the chambers/vessels it connects
Watch a valve animation cycle and identify open vs closed phases
Answer a checkpoint question on which valve prevents backflow into a given chamber

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify the great vessels entering and leaving the heart, setting up the vascular connections needed to trace circulation.
key_visuals: Full heart model with vessels extended and labeled: superior/inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta
Color-coded vessel paths (blue for deoxygenated, red for oxygenated)
Directional arrows indicating blood flow into or out of the heart
student_actions: Tap each vessel to reveal its name and whether it carries oxygenated or deoxygenated blood
Trace a finger along a vessel to confirm flow direction
Sort vessels into 'entering heart' vs 'leaving heart' categories

scenes.brief_purpose: Walk students through the right-heart pathway that sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs for gas exchange.
key_visuals: Animated blood flow path glowing blue from vena cavae through right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary arteries to the lungs
Lung icons showing gas exchange turning blood red
Pulmonary veins returning oxygenated blood toward the left atrium
student_actions: Tap sequential structures in the correct order to activate the animated blood flow
Use a slider to control the pace of the animation and observe valve timing
Complete a fill-in-the-blank sequence of the pulmonary pathway

scenes.brief_purpose: Complete the circulation story by tracing oxygenated blood from the left atrium through to the aorta and out to the body.
key_visuals: Animated blood flow glowing red from pulmonary veins through left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and into the aorta
Branching aorta extending toward a simplified body outline
Full dual-loop diagram showing both pulmonary and systemic circuits together
student_actions: Tap sequential structures in order to animate the systemic pathway
Compare pressure/force cues (thicker arrow, faster animation) to the pulmonary loop
Complete a fill-in-the-blank sequence of the systemic pathway

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate learning by having students trace the complete dual-loop circulation in one continuous animation and demonstrate mastery of structure-function relationships.
key_visuals: Complete heart model with both loops animating simultaneously in a continuous cardiac cycle
Synchronized valve opening/closing with chamber contraction
Summary diagram overlay listing chambers, valves, and vessels in circulation order
student_actions: Drag and drop all structures into the correct circulation order from vena cava to aorta
Narrate or select the correct valve at each transition point in a guided quiz
Complete a final assessment identifying structure, function, and blood oxygenation status at each step
